title: Dietary Carbohydrates: Glycaemic Index, Dietary Fibre and Trans Fats

steps.title: Industrial partial hydrogenation and trans fats
steps.tx: Formed during industrial partial hydrogenation of liquid vegetable oils to produce solid shortening and vanaspati, **industrial trans fatty acids** possess geometric trans double bonds that straighten fatty acyl chains into rigid structures. Trans fats exert a doubly deleterious atherogenic effect, simultaneously elevating circulating low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and depressing protective high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, multiplying coronary artery disease risk.
steps.say: Trans fats are created when liquid vegetable oils are chemically hardened into vanaspati ghee. They simultaneously drive up bad LDL cholesterol and drive down protective HDL cholesterol.

steps.title: Regulatory limits and India's trans-fat elimination
steps.tx: To protect cardiovascular health, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India enforces strict **trans fat regulatory limits** across all commercial fats, bakery shortenings, margarines and edible vegetable oils. Aligned with the WHO REPLACE initiative, statutory regulations capped trans fats at no more than two percent by weight of total oils, with packaged food manufacturers legally prohibited from using partially hydrogenated vegetable oils.
steps.say: The Food Safety and Standards Authority caps trans fats at two percent of total oil weight in all packaged foods, banning dangerous partially hydrogenated fats from bakery items.

rows: Lowered to 5 percent in all fats

steps.title: Dietary fibre: soluble versus insoluble components
steps.tx: The non-digestible carbohydrate fraction derived from plant cell walls constitutes **dietary fibre intake**, dividing into water-soluble and water-insoluble fractions. Insoluble fibres (cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin) from whole wheat bran and vegetable skins increase stool bulk, accelerate intestinal transit, and prevent diverticular disease; soluble fibres (pectins, beta-glucans and mucilages) from oats, fenugreek and legumes form viscous gels that blunt postprandial glycaemia.
steps.say: Dietary fibre is plant matter that resists human digestion. Insoluble wheat fibre bulks stool and prevents constipation, while soluble oat fibre forms a gel that traps sugars and cholesterol.

steps.title: Recommended fibre intake and health benefits
steps.tx: The National Institute of Nutrition prescribes an **adequate fibre recommendation** of thirty to forty grams daily for adults (or roughly fifteen grams per one thousand kilocalories ingested). In addition to preventing hemorrhoids and colonic cancer through dilution of faecal carcinogens, colonic bacterial fermentation of soluble fibre yields short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate and butyrate) that nourish colonocytes and suppress hepatic cholesterol synthesis.
steps.say: Adults need thirty to forty grams of fibre every day. Bacteria ferment soluble fibre into short-chain fatty acids that protect the bowel wall and lower liver cholesterol production.

steps.title: Glycaemic index: postprandial glucose curves
steps.tx: To rank carbohydrate foods based on their physiological impact on blood sugar, nutritionists calculate the **glycaemic index ranking**. Determined by measuring the incremental area under the two-hour blood glucose response curve following ingestion of fifty grams of available carbohydrate from a test food, it is expressed as a percentage of the response elicited by fifty grams of pure glucose or white bread.
steps.say: The glycaemic index measures how fast a food raises blood sugar compared to pure glucose over two hours. Foods with a low index release sugar slowly, preventing insulin spikes.

rows: Whole pulses (rajma, chana), barley, soy, apples
Brown rice, whole wheat roti, rolled oats, sweet potato
White polished rice, maida refined flour, cornflakes, potatoes

steps.tx: After a fifty gram carbohydrate load, white rice drives a steep postprandial glucose rise, whereas lentils produce a flatter curve across the same two hours. Nutritionists rank that difference with the **glycaemic index ranking**, calculated from the incremental area beneath the blood glucose response and compared with the response to an equal glucose or white bread load. High values mark foods that lift sugar quickly, while many pulses keep the rise lower and more spread out.

steps.title: Glycaemic load: integrating quality and portion size
steps.tx: Because the glycaemic index does not account for typical serving portions, clinicians calculate **glycaemic load assessment**, which multiplies the food's glycaemic index by the actual grams of available carbohydrate in a standard serving, divided by one hundred. A watermelon slice possesses a high glycaemic index but a low glycaemic load because it is mostly water, whereas polished white rice delivers both high index and high load.
steps.say: Glycaemic load accounts for both carbohydrate quality and serving size. A food can have a high index but a low load if it contains very little carbohydrate per serving, like watermelon.

steps.title: Recommended dietary allowances: concepts and framework
steps.tx: Public health nutrition policy is anchored by the **recommended dietary allowance**, defined as the average daily dietary intake level of a nutrient sufficient to meet the physiological requirements of nearly all (ninety-seven to ninety-eight percent) healthy individuals in a specific life stage and gender group. Computed as the Estimated Average Requirement (EAR) plus two standard deviations, RDAs incorporate biological safety margins.
steps.say: Recommended dietary allowances are set at two standard deviations above average needs. This safety buffer ensures that daily nutritional targets cover ninety-eight percent of the population.

nodes.label: Add two standard deviations (2 SD safety margin)

steps.title: Macronutrient caloric distribution standards
steps.tx: The Indian Council of Medical Research recommends a **balanced macronutrient distribution**, specifying that total daily energy should be derived fifty to sixty percent from carbohydrates (emphasizing unrefined whole grains and pulses), twenty to thirty percent from total fats (with visible fat under thirty grams), and ten to fifteen percent from dietary protein, ensuring optimal metabolic homeostasis without excessive glycaemic stress.
steps.say: Healthy daily calories should come fifty to sixty percent from complex carbohydrates, twenty to thirty percent from healthy fats, and ten to fifteen percent from protein building blocks.

steps.title: Food labelling and consumer warning systems
steps.tx: To empower consumers to make cardioprotective choices, statutory regulations mandate clear **front-of-pack nutrition labelling** on all packaged ultra-processed foods. Manufacturers must display standardized declarations of total energy, added sugars, saturated fats, trans fatty acids and sodium per serving, accompanied by warning color-coded stop symbols when nutrient thresholds for salt, trans fats or refined sugars are breached.
steps.say: Front-of-pack nutrition labels require clear disclosure of salt, saturated fat, trans fats and added sugar per serving, warning consumers before they purchase unhealthy processed snacks.
